The idea threaded throughout this report, however, is that population location/density often correlate closely with the extent of market reach, manufacturing and commercial development and potential. Population location/density are major factors used by regional/county/city planners to predict and plan future land-uses and activities. In support, the Little Report prepared for the Freight Forwarders Institute described weaknesses of using a population-mileage formula but stated that properly used it could be a reasonable proxy to represent economic activity. The evidence developed through research by the Bureau of Economics supports the thesis that while a population-mileage formula has weaknesses, it is the most accurate technique found--other than specific definition by the Commission or alternative costly methods--to define the boundaries for commercial zones and terminal areas for base municipalities.
